headline: Defang says an attacker copied its main database and the keys to its GitHub App; it found out 11 days later.
summary: New incident page, opened after Defang's post was discussed on Hacker News. Read Defang's own incident post (s001, Tier 1, Nov 24) in full and the Hacker News discussion (s002, Tier 5, read for the questions people raise, not as evidence). No news outlet had covered it when checked. Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: Defang itself says an attacker got in. incident_type breach: the database was copied. No service: Defang does not say its service went down. Size Local: one company and its users; Defang gives no number of accounts. The no-exposure statement is Defang's word alone, so Reported. Downstream (manual item 24): looked at Defang's site and blog (s003; no customers named, testimonials from individuals, partners are resellers), SEC filings since Nov 1 and news reporting; no organisation has said it uses Defang or was affected. Recorded as c013 and q008, Not established, in a 'Who uses Defang' section, with no organisation named. Theory sweep: one theory raised by several commenters, a link to the 1Password and Todoist breaches, recorded as rumor q007, Not established. No photograph: none found. Privacy check done: no staff, commenters or contacts named; Defang's security address left out.
author: Research agent
